correctness.rationale: From the exact source-normalized vertex-update generator each active edge contributes epsilon(p_i+p_j)/(4m) to degree-weighted mass drift. Finite connectivity and epsilon in (0,1) yield a.s. finite mean absorption, so Dynkin stopping gives the occupation correction. The all-state exit function is harmonic. Singleton-opinion tests force every edge to join opposite preferences. For an arbitrary linear harmonic weight, singleton-positive and singleton-negative tests give w_i=sum_{j~i}w_j/d_j; the one-dimensional Perron stationary eigenspace gives w_i proportional to d_i, and the remaining equation forces opposite preferences on each edge. Reverse implications follow directly. The star fixation and first-change exponential waiting time are exact. Standard-library rational-state enumeration independently matched 3360 drift cases, 168 iff samples and 20 fixation computations; it is not substituted for the all-n proof.

originality.rationale: The 2026 primary paper supplies the model and a same-preference active-link drift antecedent, which is explicitly credited. The independently assessed result is the exact arbitrary-finite-graph equivalence of neutral absorption, a graph/preference proper two-colouring, and existence/uniqueness of linear martingales, together with the exact occupation correction and a star neutral-odds/slow-time separation. Full accessible relevant 2026 arXiv text (including appendices) and earlier relevant sources were compared against these quantifiers; targeted literature and semantic record searches did not identify a dominating theorem. General weighted-voter literature leaves a residual equivalence risk and absence from searches is not proof of novelty.
residual_risks: Generalized or weighted voter-model literature may contain an unindexed equivalent finite-graph harmonic-function classification.
The 2026 paper already displays same-preference edge drift at approximation level; this element alone is not novel, and one implication is mathematically short.
Some related older full texts were accessible only as abstracts or excerpts; no assertion that they were exhaustively inspected.

value.rationale: The theorem identifies the sharp structural condition under which arbitrarily strong (not frozen) partisan preference bias has precisely neutral eventual consensus odds on every finite connected network. The uniqueness characterization rules out hidden linear conservation laws outside this class. The occupation correction measures bias when the criterion fails. On arbitrary-star examples a single degree-dominant agent can win with probability one half despite many opposing intrinsically biased leaves, while decision time can diverge. This is a motivated, broadly quantified structural finite-population result rather than a single toy instance or an unmotivated small enumeration.
